_comment: Source of truth for the vendored dependency bundle (vendor/deps.js, vendor/jsqr.js). Every entry's `integrity` was computed locally (sha512 of the downloaded tarball bytes) at pin time AND cross-checked against the npm registry packument's `dist.integrity` field for that exact version -- see vendor/MANIFEST for the pin date. Do not hand-edit a version or hash; use `python3 tools/vendor-deps.py --bump <pkg>@<version>`.

bitcoinjs-lib.used_as: bitcoin.{initEccLib,address,networks,payments,crypto,Transaction,Psbt} (named imports only, so esbuild tree-shakes the rest)

jsqr.used_as: default export jsQR; also vendored standalone as vendor/jsqr.js from dist/jsQR.js (see MANIFEST)

@bitcoin-js/tiny-secp256k1-asmjs.used_as: ecc (whole namespace, asm.js build -- deliberately NOT tiny-secp256k1, which ships WASM)

bip32.used_as: BIP32Factory (named import -- see vendor/entry.mjs comment on why not `import Foo from`)

shims._comment: Not imported by our own entry.mjs. bip32@4.0.0 -> wif@2.0.6 -> bs58check@2.1.2 -> create-hash -> md5.js -> hash-base -> readable-stream@2 needs the node core modules 'stream' and 'events', which esbuild --platform=browser will not auto-polyfill. Pinned and hash-verified the same way as the direct imports since their code ends up in the shipped bundle.

esbuild.note: This is the small JS wrapper tarball. The actual native binary is an OS/arch-specific optionalDependency (e.g. @esbuild/darwin-arm64@0.28.2) resolved and integrity-checked by npm itself during install -- npm's own fetcher verifies every package's shasum/integrity against registry metadata unconditionally, so per-platform binaries are covered even though this script only hash-verifies the wrapper tarball directly. See vendor/MANIFEST for the exact platform binary used on the last build.
